trust_decision.summary: Path components derived from server-controlled content (.git/HEAD 'ref:' line, directory-listing hrefs) are trusted as local-filesystem paths under temp_dst; nothing decides they stay inside temp_dst before os.path.exists/open/write and before hashes read from the resolved file are requested back from the server.

landing_point.why: Summary says 'ref/hash parsing' + 'existence oracle' + 'hex-fragment exfiltration': add_head_file_tasks takes the ref: path from HEAD, joins it into .git/logs, checks os.path.exists, reads the file and feeds 40-hex strings to add_hashes_parsed, which queues server requests.

fix_sites.entry_point: CLI `githacker --url` / GitHacker(...).start() in blind mode -> blind() -> add_head_file_tasks
CLI / GitHacker.start(), both modes -> every add_task caller (add_folder, add_packed_refs_tasks, add_hashes_parsed, add_blob_file_tasks, add_basic_file_tasks)
CLI / GitHacker.start() in sighted mode (directory listing) -> sighted() -> add_folder
same as add_folder (new same-origin helper replacing startswith(self.url))
worker thread consuming queue, reached from both modes
worker -> wget (removes ineffective '..' stripping, makedirs failure now aborts)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: githacker/__main__.py:206-228 (add_folder, sighted/directory-listing mode; separate path producer from the blind-mode ref parser the report points at)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Advisory is about ref/hash parsing in blind mode; directory-listing mode is a different feature that already has a same-prefix check and '..' stripping (githacker/__main__.py:222-227) plus a '..' sanitizer in wget (githacker/__main__.py:610-615), so it looks already defended.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate dot-prefixed path segments ('.git', '.gitignore'), pack-<sha>.pack, and ref names with '.', '+', '@' must still be queued and downloaded; reusing the existing _is_safe_ref_segment (rejects leading '.') in add_task would drop every '.git/...' task and break all dumping.
O5_coupled_behaviour.where: githacker/__main__.py:46 (leading-dot rejection) vs githacker/__main__.py:126-145 (every task starts with '.git')

O6_input_shapes: multi-level traversal embedded in one segment ('../../../etc/passwd')
NUL / control chars / newline in a segment
traversal in directory-listing directory href (recursion) vs file href
cross-origin / subdomain-spoof href (victim.com.attacker.com), scheme mismatch, outside base path

O7_producer.where: githacker/__main__.py:142 (server-supplied .git/objects/info/alternates is downloaded) consumed by git's object-store loader during `git fsck` at githacker/__main__.py:253-265; fsck output hashes go to add_hashes_parsed githacker/__main__.py:341-348

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Server-supplied .git/objects/info/alternates names an arbitrary local object directory; git fsck in temp_dst reads it and hashes from its output are requested back from the server (same existence-oracle / hex-leak property, via git's own path resolution rather than GitHacker's parsing).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is git's own documented alternates feature, not GitHacker's ref/hash parsing; the file is in the default download list on purpose and no GitHacker code joins its contents into a path.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file; the consumer is the external git binary invoked at githacker/__main__.py:254-258, far from the HEAD parser

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Parser for downloaded .git/objects/info/packs ('P pack-<sha>.pack') that queues pack names straight into add_task-like path joins / local exists checks.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: packs is already downloaded but never parsed and copy_useful_files expects .git/objects/pack (githacker/__main__.py:276); adding pack recovery is a natural next feature.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Symref reader for .git/refs/remotes/origin/HEAD ('ref: refs/remotes/origin/main') mirroring add_head_file_tasks, joining the ref into .git/logs and reading it locally.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same file format as HEAD; a maintainer would copy add_head_file_tasks for it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: FETCH_HEAD parser extracting branch names ("branch 'x' of ...") into a path without _is_safe_ref_segment.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Recent commits expand branch discovery (packed-refs, logs/HEAD); FETCH_HEAD is another listed-but-unparsed source.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal (server-controlled path components reaching local filesystem exists/read/write; existence oracle + data exfiltration back to server)

O10_build.toolchain: Python >=3.12 (pyproject.toml:6), pip deps requests, bs4, GitPython, coloredlogs; pytest; git binary for blind mode fsck/clone
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_ref_validation.py (ref-segment, wordlist and packed-refs validation, using _make_hacker at tests/test_ref_validation.py:136-144 without network); malicious-server behaviour can be exercised via mocks or a local HTTP server

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate ref_path segments only inside add_head_file_tasks (or reuse _is_safe_ref_segment in add_task, which rejects '.git' and breaks every download).

out_of_scope_notes: Fix also switches to a requests.Session with TLS verification on by default and a --insecure flag (fix.diff:69-89, 338-341); unrelated to traversal.

Sighted mode skips fsck and goes straight to git clone of temp_dst (githacker/__main__.py:179-182); other git control files from a listing (e.g. commondir) influencing local git is a separate concern, not pursued.
